test_title: SSC CPO 2023 Official Paper-I (Held On: 04 Oct, 2023 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: _______ 2005 is referred to as the ‘Right to Work’ as it guaranteed 100 days of employment in a year by the Indian Government to people who are in need of and who are able to do work.

options.text: Mahatma Gandhi Regional Employment Guarantee Act
Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act

solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) of 2005** is a pivotal social welfare measure designed to ensure that every household willing to engage in unskilled manual work receives **100 days of wage** employment annually.
 
• Enacted in 2005 and put into effect in **2006**, this act has multifaceted objectives:
 
 
• Guaranteeing one-third of the employment opportunities to women.
 
• Generating durable assets through rural works.
 
• Promoting environmental conservation through rural projects.
 
 
 
• Under the **Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005,** each State Government is mandated to introduce its own scheme.
 
• Accordingly, the** "Haryana Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme" **was established, aligning with the operational guidelines and provisions outlined in the national legislation.
 
• This scheme was officially published in the Haryana Government Gazette (Extra) on March 16, 2007, by the State Government.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme** was inaugurated by the Government of India in all **Gram Panchayats of Mahendergarh and Sirsa districts **on** February 2, 2006**.
 
• Subsequently, the scheme was extended to two additional districts, Ambala and Mewat, effective April 1, 2007.
 
• The remaining districts of the state were brought under the purview of the scheme from April 1, 2008.
 
• The primary goal of the scheme is to bolster livelihood security for rural households by offering round-the-year employment opportunities, ensuring a minimum of one hundred days of wage employment per financial year to each household volunteering for unskilled manual work.
 
• A secondary objective is the creation of assets aimed at the overall development of rural areas.
